Ellipsoids, contact points and sharp norm comparison

Written by GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), October 2026. Public domain (CC0).

A symmetric convex body contains an ellipsoid which measures every direction within a factor of . The exponent matters: a cube attains this factor in each diagonal direction. We prove the comparison by finding finitely many supporting directions whose weighted squares add to the identity. Those same directions certify maximal volume and uniqueness.

The finite algebra foundation, Sections 10.1–10.8, proves basis extension, determinants, inner products, adjoints and traces. The supplied real spectral theorem gives orthogonal diagonalization. Compactness and continuous extrema are proved in the scalar foundation, Sections 12.5–12.9. The integration foundation proves the linear volume formula. All convex-geometric arguments needed here are given below.

The constant cannot be decreased uniformly over all such bodies.
